summary: An enumerated or single-value survey number is returned isolated from its subdivision number, even when both are plainly available in the same source chunk.
preconditions: sis_multi_survey_test.txt attached (survey numbers 101, 102, 103, 104; each has 0-2 subdivisions recorded nearby).
reproduction: -> Before fix: 'The survey numbers mentioned are: 101, 102, 103. (101 (2x) mentioned more than once.)' -- no subdivision information at all.
-> Expected: each survey number paired with its own subdivision(s).
root_cause: _enumerate_entities_answer() / _single_entity_answer() in backend/services/attachment_qa.py only ever ran the survey-number regex (_ENTITY_PATTERNS['survey number']); nothing cross-referenced a survey-number match against the subdivision-number matches sitting in the same evidence text, even though the subdivision pattern already existed (built in the previous QA pass for a separate question shape).
verified_outcome: Live UI, same session: 'The survey numbers mentioned are: 101 (subdivision: 101/1); 102 (subdivision: 102/4); 103 (subdivision not specified in source); 104 (subdivision: 104/1A, 104/1B). (101 (2x) mentioned more than once.)' New functions survey_subdivision_pairs() / _render_survey_pairs_answer() / _render_survey_subdivision_table() in attachment_qa.py.
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13

summary: A survey number with MORE THAN ONE subdivision risked being narrowed to just one, or the subdivisions merged/lost, once a pairing mechanism existed -- this is the specific case the fix had to get right, not merely the simpler one-subdivision case.
preconditions: sis_multi_survey_test.txt extended with Record E: survey number 104, genuinely split into two synthetic subdivisions, 104/1A and 104/1B, both mentioned in the same record's text. No prior fixture in this project had a survey number with more than one distinct subdivision.
reproduction: 2. Send: 'List every survey number mentioned.' or 'Show all survey numbers and subdivision numbers in a table.'
-> Expected: survey 104's entry (or table rows) name BOTH 104/1A and 104/1B, never just one.
root_cause: N/A -- this was a NEW requirement with no prior broken behaviour to reproduce (no fixture existed to expose a narrowing bug). Built as a deliberate regression case for the fix in PAIR-001, to prove the pairing function does not accidentally collapse multiple subdivisions into one.
verified_outcome: survey_subdivision_pairs() correctly returns ('104', ['104/1A', '104/1B'], 1, <evidence>); the table rendering gives 104 two separate rows, one per subdivision. Verified both at the function level (test_survey_subdivision_pairing.py) and via direct plan_answer()/live UI calls.
evidence_source: direct function calls + live browser session, 2026-10-13

summary: A CSV 'list the <survey column>' projection silently dropped each row's subdivision value, even though it was present in the same row of the same file -- the deterministic CSV engine already had the full row in hand and discarded part of it.
preconditions: sis_survey_records_en.csv attached, with both synthetic_survey_no and synthetic_subdivision_no columns.
reproduction: 2. Send: 'In sis_survey_records_en.csv, list the synthetic_survey_no column.'
-> Before fix: 'row 1: 801 / row 2: 802' -- subdivision silently dropped.
-> Expected: each row's subdivision value stated alongside its survey number.
root_cause: csv_ops.execute()'s OP_FILTER-with-column projection branch always isolated to exactly the one requested column (res.value = [(n, r.get(operation.column)) ...]); nothing checked whether the requested column was itself a survey-number column with a sibling subdivision column in the same row.
verified_outcome: Live UI: 'In sis_survey_records_en.csv, list the synthetic_survey_no column.' -> '2 match(es): row 1: 801 (subdivision: 801/1) / row 2: 802 (subdivision: 802/1)'. New _sibling_subdivision_column() in csv_ops.py (header-name matching, never column position), execute() pairs the cells, render_csv_result() in attachment_qa.py renders the 3-tuple shape; a genuinely recorded '0' subdivision value (NISD files with no sub-division, per the project's own documented data convention) is preserved verbatim, never replaced with 'Not specified in source'.
evidence_source: live browser session + direct csv_ops/render_csv_result calls, 2026-10-13

summary: The task's own example phrasing, 'How many survey numbers and subdivisions are present?', did not match the occurrence-count regex at all (which required the word 'mentions'), so it fell to the default enumeration rendering instead of stating the total pair count.
reproduction: 1. Send: 'How many survey numbers and subdivisions are present?'
-> Before fix: fell to the default prose listing, no total count stated.
-> Expected: states both the unique survey-number count and the total survey/subdivision pair count.
root_cause: _OCCURRENCE_COUNT_RE / _ENUMERATE_RE in attachment_qa.py required '\bhow many\b.{0,20}\bmention' -- 'are present' / 'are there' were not recognised cues at all, and even after adding them the character gap cap (20, then 30) was too short for 'how many survey numbers and subdivisions are present' (32 characters between the two anchor phrases).
verified_outcome: _OCCURRENCE_COUNT_RE / _ENUMERATE_RE widened to also match '...are there'/'...are present', and the character gap raised to 40. 'How many survey numbers and subdivisions are present?' now correctly states 'There are 5 survey number mentions (4 unique value(s), 5 survey/subdivision pair(s)).' Verified at the function level (test_survey_subdivision_pairing.py); not independently re-verified through the live UI (only PAIR-001/003's headline cases were re-tested live after the backend restart).

summary: 'Find all subdivisions belonging to survey number 101.' -- a reverse lookup naming a SPECIFIC survey number and asking for its subdivisions -- is not a registered enumeration shape and falls through to the ordinary LLM/retrieval path, with none of this fix's pairing guarantees.
reproduction: 1. Send: 'Find all subdivisions belonging to survey number 101.'
-> Actual: handled by the generic retrieval+LLM path, not the deterministic pairing path built in this pass.
root_cause: wants_enumeration() / the entity-pairing branch in plan_answer() only fires for a bare 'survey number' question; a question that NAMES a specific survey number and asks for its subdivisions is a different shape (closer to a field lookup on a named entity) that was not built in this pass.
verified_outcome: NOT FIXED -- out of this pass's scope. Candidate direction: a new branch in plan_answer() recognising 'subdivisions of/belonging to survey <N>' and returning survey_subdivision_pairs() filtered to that one survey number.

summary: A follow-up after a paired enumeration answer ('What other subdivisions belong to it?', 'Only show unique survey numbers' expected to preserve the full subdivision list) does not resolve -- this is the SAME pre-existing follow-up-context gap already confirmed and reported, unfixed, in the previous pass.
preconditions: sis_multi_survey_test.txt attached, 'List every survey number mentioned.' already asked and answered with the new paired rendering.
reproduction: 1. Send 'List every survey number mentioned.' (gets the paired answer).
2. Send 'What is the first one?' or 'What other subdivisions belong to it?'
-> Actual: 'Nothing has been shown in this conversation yet...' -- the paired enumeration answer records no FollowupContext for the next turn to resolve against.
root_cause: Same as SIS_Upload_Extraction_Consistency_Fix_Report.md's documented, unfixed gap: _enumerate_entities_answer() / _render_survey_pairs_answer() record no follow-up context. Building this (a new FollowupContext entity kind for an entity-pair list, wired through followup_context.py and chatbot.py's _load_followup_context()) is a materially larger change than this pass's confirmed pairing defect.
verified_outcome: NOT FIXED -- explicitly out of scope, reported rather than hidden, consistent with the previous pass's handling of the same gap.
evidence_source: inherited from the previous pass's SIS_Upload_Extraction_Consistency_Fix_Report.md; not independently re-tested this pass since no code changed in this area
